title: Embed+Rerank Model Intake: Version Pinning & Profile Publication Pipeline
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end intake and publishing path for embedding and reranker models that produces canonical performance profiles and supports explicit version pinning for customers. Scope includes: (1) a standardized onboarding manifest for embedding+reranker artifacts, (2) an automated benchmark harness that emits latency, throughput, memory, and embedding quality metrics (cosine similarity on canonical eval sets), (3) profile metadata schema and storage in the model catalog, (4) API/CLI flags for customers to pin a model version and to prefer a profile tag (e.g., low-latency vs high-accuracy), and (5) Console UI for publishing/approving profiles and showing profile diffs across versions. Success criteria emphasize reproducible perf numbers, clear pin semantics, and a low-friction workflow for model owners to publish profiles.

Technical approach: package embedding and reranker models with a manifest (model.yaml) containing architecture, tokenizer, quantization info, supported sequence lengths, and expected tokenization quirks. The benchmark harness will run representative workloads (short/long queries, batch sizes) and compute token-level latency percentiles, batching efficiency, GPU memory footprint, and quality metrics (embedding cosine separability on held-out sets, reranker NDCG@10). Profiles will be stored as immutable artifacts in the catalog with a semantic tag and a small JSON summary (string fields only): perf_percentiles, recommended_batching, kv_cache_recommendation, quantization_profile, evaluation_date, and commit_id. Version pinning semantics: customers can pin to (model_id, version_id) or to (model_id, profile_tag) where profile_tag maps to the latest annotated version marked with that tag. When pinned, requests must resolve deterministically; fallbacks only occur when compatibility checks pass (tokenizer + model architecture).

Trade-offs and constraints: running full quality evals is expensive; initial rollout will compute a lightweight quality signal for rerankers (NDCG on 1k queries) and full runs will be optional nightly jobs. To keep onboarding velocity, we allow staged publishing: draft -> internal review -> public. Security/PII: onboarding harness must run on private infra for customer-provided data; this ticket excludes integration with customer KMS, deferred to next cycle.

Acceptance criteria and rollout plan are below.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New onboarding manifest accepted by catalog importer and validated in CI. 2) Benchmark harness runs reproducibly in CI for a synthetic and a real eval set and emits the profile JSON per schema. 3) Model catalog stores immutable profile artifacts and exposes a profile_tag resolution endpoint. 4) API accepts version pin parameters and returns the pinned model deterministically; unit + integration tests cover pin resolution, fallback rules, and mismatch errors. 5) Console has a minimal publish UI for profile approval and shows key perf fields. 6) Internal doc (Confluence) with instructions for model owners and a checklist for profile publication.
steps: Define model manifest schema (model.yaml) and validation rules
Build benchmark harness module: latency, throughput, memory, embedding quality (cosine) and reranker NDCG
Implement profile JSON schema and storage API in model catalog
Add API/CLI flags for version pinning and profile_tag resolution
Console: small publish/approve workflow and profile diff UI
CI: add reproducible run & snapshot testing for profiles
Docs: onboarding guide + checklist + example models
